definition: Detecting malicious activity in networks or systems — signature- and anomaly-based methods with ML used to spot novel attacks.
details: Detecting malicious activity in networks or systems — signature- and anomaly-based methods with ML used to spot novel attacks.

explainer.lead: Intrusion detection is the detection of malicious activity in networks or systems, using signature- and anomaly-based methods with machine learning used to spot novel attacks. It matters because monitored activity can be reported to administrators or collected centrally for alarm filtering.

tiers.eli5: It is like a security guard watching a building and flagging anyone doing something suspicious.
tiers.practitioner: Security engineers deploy network-based and host-based detection, combining signature-based recognition of bad patterns with anomaly-based detection that relies on models of good traffic. A pitfall is false alarms, which is why SIEM systems apply alarm filtering to distinguish malicious activity from noise.
tiers.paperLevel: An IDS monitors a network or systems for malicious activity or policy violations; common classifications are network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) and host-based intrusion detection systems (HIDS), and detection approaches include signature-based, anomaly-based (often using machine learning), and reputation-based methods. Limits: anomaly detection can flag benign deviations, so filtering is needed.

explainer.example: An NIDS analyzes incoming network traffic and flags an exploitation attempt by matching a known bad pattern, then reports it to a SIEM system.
